nodes.text: TXN-C04-FIRST and TXN-C04-SECOND are two separate posted USD 64.18 ecommerce transactions, not duplicate views: they have distinct transaction IDs and timestamps four days apart, and they occupy separate CLEARS sequence positions (1 and 2) against the same approved USD 128.36 authorization. Both are tied to the same card, merchant, and order; the order totals USD 128.36 for two lamps and has two separately dated shipments, supporting two captures rather than a display duplication.

nodes.text: TXN-C04-FIRST and TXN-C04-SECOND are not independent payment contexts: both $64.18 USD clearings use the same approved authorization AUT-C04 (authorized for $128.36), with clearing sequences 1 and 2, and the same Visa card CRD-C04 (last four 0404). Both are at merchant MER-C04 (Parcelwick Home), tied to the same order ORD-C04 and separate shipment records SHP-C04-A/B; no descriptor, device, IP, terminal, or token metadata is present to distinguish them.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.text: ORD-C04 is a single USD order for 2 x Harlow brass floor lamp totaling $128.36, not one lamp totaling $64.18. It is linked by E-0507358 to TXN-C04-FIRST and by E-0507362 to TXN-C04-SECOND; both are separate posted $64.18 ecommerce purchases on 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-09, respectively. Both clear the same approved $128.36 authorization AUT-C04 through E-0507357 (seq 1) and E-0507361 (seq 2). No REFUNDS relationship or separate refund/reversal/credit transaction is linked to either charge; the graph contains no offset. The order also has two shipments, SHP-C04-A and SHP-C04-B, via E-0507363 and E-0507365, supporting two ordered units. Customer evidence is limited to the dispute intake in DSP-2026-90004 (E-0507369), which asserts duplicate charging but is not proof of an offset.

nodes.text: TXN-C04-FIRST and TXN-C04-SECOND were intended split captures of $64.18 each, not an accidental duplicate: both posted transactions clear the same approved $128.36 authorization, both belong to ORD-C04 for two Harlow brass floor lamps, and the order has two separately shipped parcels delivered to the customer's home address. The disputed second charge is therefore supported and no credit is due.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Durable duplicate-processing pattern: when multiple posted clearings are linked to one order, their amounts sum exactly to the order total, and fulfillment records show the corresponding number of units or shipments, treat them as split/partial clearings rather than duplicate billing; shared authorization and explicit clearing sequence positions strengthen that conclusion. Missing descriptor, device, IP, terminal, or token metadata does not by itself establish duplicate billing. Reassess if reliable records show a one-unit order, an excess capture, or a later credit/refund.
